definition: One complete pass through the entire training dataset.
details: During training, models typically see the full dataset multiple times (multiple epochs) so weights can be updated repeatedly via gradient descent. Too few epochs can underfit; too many can overfit without regularization.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. In plain words: One complete pass through the entire training dataset. Here is how it actually plays out: During training, models typically see the full dataset multiple times (multiple epochs) so weights can be updated repeatedly via gradient descent. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Epoch.
